title: Patient factors in copper IUD fragmentation requiring hysteroscopic removal

answers.study/department: Obstetrics and Gynaecology, UHN gynaecology clinics. Team is the PI, one OB/GYN resident (Dr. Neha Singh) and three medical students who do the chart review.
answers.study/summary: Retrospective chart review of patients who had a copper IUD (ParaGard) removed and needed hysteroscopy to retrieve retained fragments. We will abstract demographics, IUD characteristics, comorbidities, imaging findings and pre-, intra- and post-procedure details from Epic into UHN REDCap and look for patient factors associated with fragmentation. Results go to a national reproductive and gynecologic conference, then a manuscript.
answers.classification/question: Which patient factors are associated with copper IUD fragmentation on removal that needs hysteroscopy to retrieve the pieces? We hypothesize that uterine anatomic abnormalities and longer duration of ParaGard use are associated with fragmentation. Goal is better counselling of patients choosing a copper IUD.
answers.classification/cohort/population: Adults (18+) who had an IUD removal at UHN that needed a subsequent hysteroscopy to retrieve retained IUD fragments, in the last 20 years. Cases found by a Data Services query on the procedure and diagnosis codes listed in the protocol (hysteroscopic removal of impacted foreign body, IUD removal, displacement and mechanical complication codes), then confirmed by chart review.
answers.classification/cohort/dateRationale: The protocol covers the last 20 years. Fragmentation needing hysteroscopy is rare, so we need the whole window to get enough cases. Counted back from the end of September 2026.
answers.classification/cohort/exclusionsWhy: Under 18 excluded, same as the original protocol. Most UHN gynaecology patients are adults anyway.
answers.classification/sources/sourceDetails: UHN Epic EMR: clinic notes, procedure and operative notes, ultrasound and X-ray reports, problem list and medical history. Case-finding list from UHN Data Services using CPT 58562 and the ICD-10 codes in the protocol (Z30.432, T83.32, T83.39, T83.9XXA etc.). No CAPCR numbers, these are clinical systems.
answers.identifiability/fields: Age at removal, BMI, gravidity and parity, comorbidities, IUD type and duration of use, reason for removal, imaging findings, details of the removal and hysteroscopy, complications. MRN is only used during chart review to confirm eligibility and is removed from the REDCap record once extraction is done. No names, addresses or health card numbers.
answers.identifiability/reidentification: MRNs deleted from REDCap after extraction, each patient is only a REDCap record number after that. Access limited to the study team. All results reported in aggregate.
answers.handling/storage/access: PI, the resident and the three medical students only. UHN REDCap project, user rights set by the PI, UHN accounts. Remote chart review only over the UHN VPN. The biostatistician gets an export without MRNs.
answers.handling/results/incidental: Not expected. Records only, aggregate results, nobody is contacted. If a chart shows something concerning the PI will raise it with the treating team.
answers.digital/usage: Standard UHN REDCap project for chart abstraction. Only the study team enters data, no surveys or patient-facing forms.
answers.resources/other: One case-finding query from Data Services. Biostatistics support for the descriptive stats and logistic regression, about 2 months.

weaknesses: Identifiability and consent: identifiability/arrival is 'anonymized' with keyHolder 'none' and consent/sought is 'notApplicable', but the protocol (p. 6) has the team identify patients by MRN in the chart during eligibility and extraction. The data is directly identifying in the team's hands, a waiver is needed, and the form skips the waiver section entirely.

Sensitive category not ticked: sensitivity/categories is 'none' although the whole dataset is contraception and gynaecological procedures (reproductive care). breachHarm 'minimal' follows from the same blind spot.

End date in the recent past: classification/cohort/endDate is 2026-09-30, a month before submission. The protocol's 20-year window was anchored to its May 2024 version; moving it forward brings in recent patients still in follow-up who could be asked.
No small-cell rule: handling/results/reporting is 'aggregate' with no suppression threshold, for a rare complication at one site.
Supporting detail: the variable list keeps exact insertion, removal and hysteroscopy dates, which identifiability/fields does not mention.

From the protocol itself, not built in: the exclusion criteria remove every removal without fragmentation, so there is no comparison group for the planned logistic regression; case-finding uses US CPT and ICD-10-CM codes; the protocol contradicts itself on sharing de-identified data (p. 6).

screening.summary: A single-site chart review of a rare gynaecological complication, kept in UHN REDCap with no data leaving UHN. The main problem is that the form calls the data anonymized and asks for neither consent nor a waiver, while the team reads charts by MRN; the reproductive care category is also not ticked. As written, the analysis has no comparison group, so the stated question can't be answered from this cohort.

assessments.summary: Research, records only, retrospective chart review. The purpose, the absence of contact and the clinical data sources agree with the protocol.
The data is directly identifying while the team extracts it, not anonymized, and the retained fields include exact procedure dates.

comments.text: The form says the data arrives anonymized with no key, but the team itself finds each patient by MRN in Epic to confirm eligibility and extract the data, and only removes the MRN afterwards. That is directly identifying data in the team's hands, so 'not applicable' for consent does not hold.
comments.suggestion: Change the arrival to directly identifying and the consent answer to a waiver request, then argue each waiver condition.
comments.quote: Individual subjects will be identified by their UKHS medical record numbers during the initial chart review and data collection phase.

comments.text: The variable list keeps exact dates of insertion, removal and hysteroscopy, which the identifiers answer doesn't mention. For a rare complication at one hospital, exact procedure dates plus age could single someone out, so 'unlikely' to be recognized is optimistic.
comments.suggestion: Compute duration of use and the removal-to-hysteroscopy interval at extraction, keep the year only, and drop the exact dates.

assessments.summary: No waiver is requested because the data is treated as non-identifiable; once that is corrected the waiver conditions need to be argued.

comments.text: Once the identifiability answer is corrected, a waiver is needed. Many patients in a 20-year gynaecology cohort, especially recent ones, are likely still seen at UHN, so impracticability can't rest on cohort size alone, and the cohort may be far smaller than the 700 maximum.
comments.suggestion: Request a waiver and say why consent is impracticable for this cohort specifically, and why chart access by MRN is essential.

assessments.summary: The whole dataset is reproductive care, which the form doesn't declare.

comments.text: The study is about contraception and gynaecological procedures, which is reproductive care, but the sensitive categories answer is 'none of these'. Ticking it also opens the question of whether anyone placed to see the risks has been consulted.
comments.suggestion: Tick reproductive care and answer the follow-up question on input.
comments.quote: Intrauterine devices (IUD) have been increasing in popularity as a contraception method over the past twenty years

assessments.summary: The window runs to a month before submission.

comments.text: The end date is 30 September 2026. The protocol's 20-year window was written in May 2024; counting it from today pulls in patients who had a hysteroscopy in the last few weeks and are probably still in follow-up, who could reasonably be asked for consent.
comments.suggestion: End the window at least a year back, for example at the protocol's May 2024 date, or explain why the recent cases are needed.

assessments.summary: The cohort only contains patients with the outcome, so the planned association analysis can't be done; case-finding codes also need translating for UHN.

comments.text: The exclusion criteria remove every patient whose IUD came out without fragmentation or without hysteroscopy, so everyone in the cohort has the outcome. Logistic regression of fragmentation on patient factors, and the chi-square and t-test comparisons, need a group without fragmentation to compare against.
comments.suggestion: Add a comparison group, such as copper IUD removals without fragmentation over the same period, or restate the aim as a descriptive case series.
comments.quote: patients who undergo IUD removal without requiring hysteroscopy, patient who undergo IUD removal without fragmentation of device

comments.text: Case-finding uses CPT 58562 and US ICD-10-CM codes such as T83.9XXA. UHN codes procedures in CCI and diagnoses in ICD-10-CA, so the query as written may find few or no cases.
comments.suggestion: Ask Data Services to map the code list to CCI and ICD-10-CA before the query is run.
comments.quote: Subjects will be recruited from KUMC via chart query using ICD-10 codes and CPT codes.

assessments.summary: Aggregate reporting with no suppression rule, for a rare outcome at a single site.

comments.text: Results will be aggregate with no small-cell rule. Tables by uterine anomaly, IUD type or complication will likely have counts of one or two, and the abstract goes to a national conference.
comments.suggestion: Set a threshold, for example suppress counts under 6 as ICES does, and apply it to abstracts and posters as well as the manuscript.
comments.quote: All data will be presented in aggregate without identifying information.

assessments.summary: Nothing leaves UHN by design, but the protocol is ambiguous about releasing de-identified data with the publication.

comments.text: The protocol says de-identified data and results will be shared via publication, but also that no de-identified data leaves the site, and the form lists no other uses. If the journal's data-sharing policy leads to posting a dataset, that is a disclosure outside UHN the form doesn't cover.
comments.suggestion: Confirm that only aggregate results are published, or declare the dataset release and how it would be anonymized.
comments.quote: After completion of the study, de-identified data and results will be shared with participants via publication of research results.

assessments.summary: UHN REDCap with team-only access and a set retention period is appropriate; the breach harm is understated.

comments.text: Breach harm is given as minimal. During extraction the REDCap project holds MRNs next to contraceptive and gynaecological history, and three medical students work on it remotely; a breach at that stage would expose reproductive care details.
comments.suggestion: List re-identification and stigma as possible harms, and set a date by which the MRNs are deleted.

assessments.summary: One age exclusion with little effect at an adult hospital; the team hasn't taken the IDEA courses.

comments.text: Under-18s are excluded and the protocol gives no reason. At UHN this probably removes very few patients, but adolescents do use copper IUDs, so the findings may not apply to them.
comments.suggestion: Note the age limit as a limitation in the manuscript.

assessments.summary: The study uses UHN REDCap, a UHN-hosted service, with no integrations or external tools, and data stays within UHN. Nothing to flag.
